title: Stroke: history or residual deficits
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's past stroke and any residual deficits.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for expressive aphasia.

HPI
Pt is an 87 y.o. female presenting for follow-up of residual expressive aphasia. Pt reports consistent difficulty with word-finding but notes she is able to communicate basic needs. History is significant for a past ischemic stroke. Pt denies any new neurological symptoms.

Medication List
Lisinopril 10mg daily
Atorvastatin 20mg daily

Exam
Gen: Well-appearing, alert, and oriented.
Neuro: Speech characterized by expressive aphasia. No motor deficits noted.
Vitals: BP 132/78, HR 72, RR 16, Temp 98.6F, SpO2 98% on RA.
Physical: RRR, CTAB, WNL.

Assessment
1. Expressive aphasia secondary to prior ischemic stroke. Pt is stable but continues to struggle with verbal fluency.

Plan
1. Continue current medications.
2. Speech therapy referral for continued verbal practice.
3. F/u in 3 months to monitor progress.

Electronically signed,
R. Mensah, DO
10/14/2026
explanations: Residual aphasia from a past ischemic stroke: I69.320, a sequela code (no HCC in V28).

distractors.why: A residual deficit is documented: code the sequela (I69.-), not Z86.73.
I63 codes are for the acute stroke episode only.
